task: This is a synthetic newspaper-writing exercise using fictional reporting notes. Use only the supplied reporting notes. Write from the reporting snapshot as of August 28, 2026. Write a headline and a 450–650-word AP-style newspaper news update on Sedge Row Paper's water-reuse investment and the costs and claims attached to it.

facts.text: Sedge Row Paper's board approved a $5.6 million water-reuse installation on Friday, Aug. 28, 2026.
Construction at the Dovewick mill is scheduled to begin in November and take eight months.
The mill currently draws an average of 900,000 gallons of fresh water a production day, according to its metered annual report.
The equipment supplier projects a reduction to 540,000 gallons at the same paper output, a target decrease of 40%.
That projection is not a measured result from the unbuilt installation.
The system will filter process water for reuse but will still require fresh water and a controlled discharge stream.
Company engineer Teri Holt said dissolved salts limit how often the same water can circulate.
The project includes new pumps that will increase electricity use; the company has not published a net energy or emissions calculation.
The mill expects its fresh-water purchase bill to fall but has not disclosed a verified payback period.
The budget includes a $1.2 million manufacturing-efficiency grant and $4.4 million in company borrowing.
Dovewick Water Authority has confirmed that the project does not itself require higher household water charges.
The authority has not promised that industrial savings will produce a cut in residential rates.
Mill employees will receive training for three new water-treatment operator assignments filled from existing staff.
Holt said, "Reusing more water is not the same as never needing another gallon."
River-users association chair Inna Cole supports reduced withdrawals but wants public comparisons at similar production levels.
Cole said, "A quieter mill uses less water too. We need to know what it took to make the same amount of paper."
The company's plan provides for monthly water-use reporting during the first operating year.
The mill's existing water authorization remains in place; the environmental office has requested updated discharge-design details.
The mill makes packaging paper from recovered fiber and replaced its pulping equipment in 2016.
The record contains no measured change in river wildlife, water quality or neighborhood health attributable to the project.

forbidden_additions: A measured 40% reduction or a completely closed water loop
Guaranteed household rate cuts, quantified net emissions benefits or demonstrated wildlife recovery
